data.title: Self-Identification and Re-Infection Checks
data.summary: The sample checks for evidence of its own prior execution on the host — a mutex, a marker file, a registry value — to avoid re-infecting an already-compromised system or running multiple instances concurrently.
data.description:
This is a bookkeeping check rather than an anti-analysis one: a named mutex or semaphore
that a second launch checks for and exits on finding, or a marker file/registry value
written on first run and checked on every subsequent one. Its practical value to the
analyst is as a reliable, family-specific identifier — the mutex name in particular is
often reused unchanged across a family's samples and campaigns.
data.recommendation:
* Record the mutex name, marker file path, or registry value checked; it is frequently a durable, family-specific identifier reusable in future hunting.
* Use the same marker as a cheap infection indicator across the environment — hosts with it present are confirmed infected without needing to re-run full analysis.
* Where the check can be forced to fail, use it to trigger re-execution of initial-access logic for analysis, rather than relying on finding a clean host.
data.short_recommendation: Record the mutex or marker checked; it is frequently a durable, family-specific infection indicator.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Checked for a named mutex on startup and exited immediately if a prior instance already held it.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Created and checked a named mutex to detect and skip re-infection of an already-compromised host.
